# Implementation Plan: codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` (Copilot CLI member, v1.8.11 caller-engine-default) on 2026-05-29. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement/plan.md`.*

## Overview

`pnpm sync-ralph-state`, `pnpm overview`, `pnpm overview:build`, and `pnpm sync-ralph-state:watch` in codexu currently dispatch through `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` — a Node resolver wrapper that locates the installed `ralph-overview` plugin's own `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` and spawns it. The wrapper is **gitignored** (`/bin/` in `.gitignore`), so the in-session 2026-05-29 patch that added Copilot CLI install-path support (`~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/`) only lives on this one machine. A fresh Copilot-only clone of codexu would fail `pnpm sync-ralph-state` because:

1. `package.json` scripts call `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs <sub>` — but `bin/` is gitignored, so there is no `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` after `git clone`.
2. The ralph-overview plugin's own `scripts/init-consumer.mjs` would emit `package.json` scripts of the form `node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo .` — but `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is Claude-Code-only and is not exported by Copilot CLI (verified against the [Copilot CLI plugin reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference) on 2026-05-29; Copilot exports only `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION`, `COPILOT_LOADER_PID`, `COPILOT_RUN_APP`, and `COPILOT_HOME`).

The goal is to make `pnpm sync-ralph-state` and `pnpm overview` work on a fresh clone of codexu under **both** Claude Code AND Copilot CLI sessions, without per-developer shell-rc setup, and without the gitignored-wrapper drift problem.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

- **`D:/harness-efforts/codexu/bin/ralph-overview.mjs`** (gitignored; 130 lines) — Node wrapper. Cascade order: `$RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT` → `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview` → `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/<latest>` → `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/<latest>` → **`~/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit/ralph-overview/`** (added in-session, gitignored) → `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview` (local-dev fallback). After resolution, spawns `pluginRoot/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` with stdio inherit, defaulting `--repo` to the consumer git root.
- **`D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.gitignore` line 114** — `/bin/` is the offending entry. Originally added because the directory was described as "per-machine symlink/junction dir" (the comment is now stale — the file is a real Node script, not a junction).
- **`D:/harness-efforts/codexu/package.json` lines 10-15** — five scripts use the wrapper:
  ```json
  "overview":                 "node bin/ralph-overview.mjs dev",
  "overview:dev":             "node bin/ralph-overview.mjs dev",
  "overview:build":           "node bin/ralph-overview.mjs build",
  "overview:build:preview":   "cross-env OVERVIEW_BUILD_SAFE_NAME=1 node bin/ralph-overview.mjs build",
  "sync-ralph-state":         "node bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync",
  "sync-ralph-state:watch":   "node bin/ralph-overview.mjs watch"
  ```
- **`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs` lines 10-15** — the plugin's hard-coded `PACKAGE_SCRIPTS` constant:
  ```js
  const PACKAGE_SCRIPTS = Object.freeze({
      overview:                  'node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs dev --repo .',
      'overview:build':          'node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs build --repo .',
      'sync-ralph-state':        'node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo .',
      'sync-ralph-state:watch':  'node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs watch --repo .',
  })
  ```
  Only written when `addPackageJsonScripts: true` is passed to `initConsumer({...})`. The `overview-init` skill defaults to `addPackageJsonScripts: false`, so most consumers never get these emitted.
- **`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs` lines 9, 29** — the plugin's own bin computes `pluginRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')` (i.e. self-locating from its own file), then exports `RALPH_OVERVIEW_PLUGIN_ROOT=pluginRoot` to child processes. That means once you can invoke the plugin's bin at all, downstream plugin processes don't need `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`.
- **`D:/harness-efforts/codexu/AGENTS.md` "Copilot migration milestone" block, follow-up (d)** — explicitly flags this gap. Two proposed remediations: re-run `overview-init` to regenerate scripts in plugin's modern form (Option A), OR un-ignore `/bin/` and commit the wrapper (Option B). This plan adopts a hybrid that addresses both the codexu-immediate and plugin-ecosystem-long-term axes.

### Technical Constraints

- **Copilot CLI exports NO plugin-path env var.** Verified 2026-05-29 against [docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference). `COPILOT_HOME` is the user-config override (defaults to `~/.copilot/`) but is not a plugin root — the install path is constructible (`$COPILOT_HOME/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/`) but no CLI subcommand or env var exposes it directly.
- **Plugin install paths differ by engine:**
  - Claude Code: `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/` (versioned subdir, multiple installs may coexist).
  - Copilot CLI: `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/` (single live copy, no per-version subdir, overwritten in place on update).
- **PNPM scripts run through `sh -c` on Unix and `cmd /c` on Windows.** Bash-style `${VAR:-default}` expansion works on Unix shells but NOT on Windows `cmd`. PowerShell users are unaffected because pnpm uses `cmd /c` regardless of the user's interactive shell. Verified: codexu's current `cross-env` usage in `overview:build:preview` works because pnpm shells out cross-platform-safely.
- **Plugin's existing self-located bin works fine** once you can reach it. The bottleneck is purely "how does the consumer's `package.json` script know the plugin's install path?"
- **AGENTS.md "lead-stays-on-main" rule** — this plan was authored in a worktree at `D:/harness-efforts/codexu-plan-wrapper-retirement` on branch `ralph/plan-codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement`, leaving the primary codexu working dir on `main`. The impl phase must follow the same worktree convention.

### Options Analysis

#### Option A — Re-run `overview-init --addPackageJsonScripts force` to regenerate `package.json` scripts in the plugin's direct-path form

Writes `"sync-ralph-state": "node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`.

- **Pros:** zero codexu-local code; uses the plugin's canonical pattern as-is.
- **Cons:** Breaks under Copilot CLI (no `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). On Windows + PowerShell + Copilot, the shell expansion would leave the literal `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` substring in the path and `node` would error with "Cannot find module ...". Verified by inspection of [`scripts/init-consumer.mjs` line 11-14](D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/scripts/init-consumer.mjs); the bash variable expansion is unconditional.
- **Verdict:** ❌ Not viable. Single-engine-only.

#### Option B — Un-ignore `/bin/` in codexu's `.gitignore` and commit the existing wrapper

Removes the `/bin/` line from `.gitignore`, commits `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (including the 2026-05-29 Copilot install path addition), and leaves `package.json` scripts pointing at `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs` (no change).

- **Pros:**
  - Ships today (zero plugin work; no version bump needed).
  - Every machine cloning codexu — Claude or Copilot — gets a working wrapper on first checkout.
  - The wrapper already handles every known plugin install path including the local-dev fallback at `D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/` (useful for plugin-author iteration without re-installing).
  - The wrapper is small (130 LoC), self-contained, well-commented, and rarely needs to change once committed.
  - No migration burden: existing developers can just `git pull` and the local-machine wrapper will be overwritten by the now-tracked version (which is identical for everyone with the in-session patch applied, and harmlessly different for those without).
- **Cons:**
  - Doesn't help **other** consumers of the ralph-overview plugin who hit the same Copilot-path gap. They'd each have to author their own wrapper.
  - Comment on `.gitignore` line 113 ("Per-machine symlink/junction dir") is now incorrect and must be updated/removed.
  - Codexu carries 130 LoC of resolver logic that arguably belongs upstream.
- **Verdict:** ✅ Pragmatic short-term fix. **Adopted as the codexu impl scope of this plan.**

#### Option C — Push cross-engine awareness UPSTREAM into the plugin's `scripts/init-consumer.mjs`

Three sub-strategies:

- **C1 — Emit a consumer-side wrapper at install time.** `overview-init` writes a tiny `bin/ralph-overview.mjs` resolver into the consumer repo (essentially Option B's wrapper, but plugin-generated + plugin-versioned). `PACKAGE_SCRIPTS` point at `node bin/ralph-overview.mjs <sub>` (no env-var dependency).
  - Pros: One canonical wrapper across all consumers; consumers who run `overview-init --force` after a plugin upgrade get bug fixes for free; plugin tests can assert the wrapper resolves correctly under simulated Claude + Copilot install layouts.
  - Cons: Consumer repos now ship a generated file that's tracked in git (creates a "regenerate the wrapper" workflow on plugin upgrades). The wrapper is plugin-version-aware but the consumer commits it manually — drift is possible if the wrapper logic changes faster than consumers re-init.
- **C2 — Emit `package.json` scripts using a cross-shell inline Node resolver.** Something like `"sync-ralph-state": "node -e \"import('node:fs').then(...)\" sync --repo ."` — resolves the plugin at script invocation time without any wrapper file.
  - Pros: No tracked wrapper file; entirely self-contained.
  - Cons: Ugly, hard to debug, and the inline JS quickly exceeds what fits inside a JSON string. Cross-shell quoting on Windows + cmd + PowerShell is a known minefield.
- **C3 — Emit `package.json` scripts with shell parameter expansion: `"node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$HOME/.copilot/installed-plugins/ai-developer-toolkit}/ralph-overview/bin/ralph-overview.mjs sync --repo ."`.
  - Pros: No new file; reads cleanly.
  - Cons: `${VAR:-default}` expansion only works in bash-family shells. Pnpm shells out via `cmd /c` on Windows, so the literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-...}` string would not expand — breaks every Windows consumer. Even on macOS/Linux, you'd hard-code the Copilot install path layout into every consumer's `package.json` and miss future install-path changes.

- **Verdict on C:** ✅ Right architectural answer for the ecosystem, but takes a plugin version bump + adoption cycle.
- **Recommended sub-strategy:** **C1** — for the reasons above and because the plugin can ship the wrapper with unit-test coverage of every install layout (something codexu's bin/ wrapper currently lacks). **Filed as a separate follow-up brainstorm/plan task** (`ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper`) per the AGENTS.md "dual-repo plans don't chain into `/implement-with-ralph` blindly" rule; this plan's impl phase remains codexu-only (Option B).

#### Option D — Upstream feature request to the GitHub Copilot CLI team

Long-term cleanest solution: add `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT_<KEBAB-PLUGIN-NAME>` env vars (parity with Claude Code's `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) OR a `copilot plugin path <plugin-name>` subcommand. Not blocking; pursued in parallel as an external dependency.

### Recommended Path

**Hybrid B + C1 + D, executed in three independent tracks:**

1. **NOW (this plan's impl phase — codexu only):** Option B. Un-ignore `/bin/`, commit the wrapper, fix the stale `.gitignore` comment, update AGENTS.md follow-up (d) to mark it resolved, and add a manual cross-engine smoke-test record. Ships in one PR, unblocks fresh Copilot clones today.
2. **NEXT (separate plan, ralph-overview plugin):** Option C1. Spawn a new brainstorm/plan task `ralph-overview-init-consumer-cross-engine-wrapper` that updates `scripts/init-consumer.mjs` to emit a consumer-side wrapper + cross-engine `PACKAGE_SCRIPTS`, with plugin-side test coverage of every install layout. When C1 ships (plugin v2.5.0+), codexu can re-run `overview-init --force` to replace its hand-committed wrapper with the plugin-emitted one and stay in sync.
3. **PARALLEL (external):** Option D. File a feature request with the Copilot CLI team. Draft text below (this plan only includes the draft — operator decides when/whether to file).

## Suggested Decomposition

This is a small, tightly-coupled change. **One parallel cluster sufficient.** All four codexu-side stories (1, 2, 3, 4) touch different files (`.gitignore` + `bin/ralph-overview.mjs`, `AGENTS.md`, new file under `.ralph/jobs/`, `plans/overview-data.js`) and have no execution ordering between them. Story 5 is plan-content only (already shipped by this document landing on main).

**Cluster A (single member):** Stories 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 in one impl pass on a single worktree off `ralph/plan-codexu-bin-ralph-overview-wrapper-retirement` (or its sibling impl branch). Estimated touch surface: ~5 files, ~80 LoC of churn.

There is no benefit to splitting these across multiple impl members — the surface is too small, and Story 4 (overview-data.js edit) is a 1-line addition that wants the same commit as the new task it references.

## Reference Artifacts

### Option D — Draft feature request for the GitHub Copilot CLI team

> **Title:** Expose installed plugin paths to scripts (parity with Claude Code's `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`)
>
> **Problem:**
> Claude Code exports `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` to every command it invokes, which lets package-manager scripts (npm/pnpm) reference plugin binaries with stable, engine-aware paths — e.g. `"sync-ralph-state": "node $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/<plugin>/bin/<entrypoint>.mjs sync"`. Cross-engine consumers of the same plugin from Copilot CLI sessions cannot use that script form because Copilot CLI does not export an equivalent env var. The only environment hints Copilot exposes today are `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI_BINARY_VERSION`, `COPILOT_LOADER_PID`, `COPILOT_RUN_APP`, and `COPILOT_HOME` ([reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference), 2026-05-29). `COPILOT_HOME` points at the user-config root but doesn't directly name plugin install locations, and consumers shouldn't have to hard-code the `installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/` layout — that's an implementation detail that may change.
>
> Without an equivalent, every cross-engine consumer needs a custom resolver wrapper checked into their repo, which fragments the ecosystem and increases the maintenance burden on plugin authors.
>
> **Proposed solutions (any one would close the gap):**
> 1. **Env var per plugin:** Export `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT_<KEBAB_PLUGIN_NAME>=...absolute-install-path...` for every installed plugin at session start. Mirrors how some CI providers expose per-secret env vars. Pro: zero-API surface; matches Claude Code's pattern.
> 2. **Single env var:** Export `COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT=<dir-containing-installed-plugins>` analogous to `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. Plugin authors then reference `$COPILOT_PLUGIN_ROOT/<marketplace>/<plugin>/bin/<entrypoint>.mjs`. Pro: small env footprint.
> 3. **CLI subcommand:** Add `copilot plugin path <plugin-name>` that prints the absolute install root to stdout. Scripts call it via command substitution: `node $(copilot plugin path ralph-overview)/bin/<entrypoint>.mjs sync`. Pro: stable contract, easy to compose. Con: extra subprocess per script invocation.
>
> **Concrete use case (the codexu / ralph-overview pair):** The `ralph-overview` plugin (published in the `gim-home/ai-developer-toolkit` marketplace) ships a Node bin dispatcher that consumers invoke from `pnpm` scripts. Today the plugin's `overview-init` skill emits package.json scripts that hard-code `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. Those scripts break on Copilot CLI. We've worked around it with a consumer-side resolver wrapper, but every new consumer of the plugin pays that cost.
>
> **Workaround until then:** Consumer-side Node resolver wrapper that probes both engine install layouts; details at https://github.com/Evyatar108/codexu/tree/main/bin/ralph-overview.mjs (post-merge link).

## Open Questions

1. **Story 1 docstring rewrite — is the local-dev fallback (`D:/ai-developer-toolkit/plugins/ralph-overview/`) still wanted?** Argument for: useful when iterating on the plugin itself without re-installing. Argument against: codexu doesn't own the plugin path and shouldn't hard-code an absolute machine-specific path. **Recommendation:** keep the fallback but reword the comment to call out that it's intentionally machine-specific and harmless when the dir doesn't exist (current behavior — `existsPluginAt` returns false, cascade falls through to `resolvePluginRoot() === null` → friendly error). Impl member can confirm during Story 1.
2. **Story 4 task `scope` value — what's the right workstream id?** Codexu uses workstreams like `infra`, `ralph`, `plugin`. The impl member should grep `plans/overview-data.js` for existing scope values and pick whichever matches the C1 task's primary surface (ralph-overview plugin). If unclear, leave a `// TODO scope` comment and the next bookkeeping pass can fix it without blocking.
3. **Operator wants Option D filed when?** Not blocking. The draft text in this plan is ready to copy-paste. Operator can decide cadence — could file immediately, could batch with other Copilot CLI feedback.
